Tech Report: Forget Butter And Oil: Cook Steak In This Rich Ingredient For A Better Crust & Beefier Flavor

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (425 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Foodrepublic

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When preparing steak, cooks often focus on selecting the best cut, then preparing it with a specific method to an ideal doneness.
  • Industry observers note that so — what is beef tallow?
  • In a recent development, in parallel, beef tallow helps create a mouthwatering crust.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When preparing steak, cooks often focus on selecting the best cut, then preparing it with a specific method to an ideal doneness. Less emphasis is placed on the fat employed for the task — although what you pour into the pan also impacts both the flavor and texture of your meal. So skip standard pantry staples like butter and oil, and try a version with beef tallow instead.

Industry observers note that so — what is beef tallow? It's essentially rendered beef fat, an ingredient that lends numerous advantages to steak night. Foremost is the ultra-savory profile: Tallow is made by slowly cooking down beef trimmings, resulting in a rich, meaty taste. This staple works as a flavor enhancer in addition to a cooking medium, complementing the deep, savory character of steak. And if you buy a higher-quality grass-fed variety, you may impart even more complexity, introducing earthy and grassy notes to your dining experience.

In a recent development, in parallel, beef tallow helps create a mouthwatering crust. The ingredient boasts a higher smoke point than butter and some other fats. So whether you're searing on high heat or finishing the steak in the oven, the fat can withstand high temperatures, enabling browning and Maillard reactions that create a terrific crust. That adds up to an elevated steak experience, all from swapping out the fat that goes into the pan.

Preparing a steak with beef tallow doesn't require any special accommodations. The fat is solid at room temperature and can be shelf-stable when properly stored, making it an easy pantry addition. You'll only need about a tablespoon per portion: Simply spoon the tallow into the skillet, where it'll melt and cover the cooking surface. It's a cooking medium that's especially effective on cast iron — whether a griddle or a pan — as it can also be used to season the cookware. You can also use tallow when grilling by coating both the cut itself and the grill grates with a thin layer of beef fat.

Recent findings suggest that any steak cut can be prepared in tallow; just note that it lends a rich flavor. So if you're making a mild-tasting filet mignon, for example, the addition could be overpowering. It's better to pair tallow with robust cuts like a ribeye, porterhouse, or Upcoming York strip, thereby producing an especially beef-forward meal. Otherwise, there's no need to worry about the details. Simply add a spoonful to your pan and sear away; this staple makes for a dependably delicious steak experience.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that eBPF (Extended Berkeley Packet Filter) is a powerful network and performance analysis tool widely used in the Linux kernel. eBPF allows developers to dynamically load, enhancement, and run user-defined code without restarting the kernel or modifying the kernel source code. This feature enables eBPF to provide high flexibility and performance, making it widely applicable in network and system performance analysis. The same applies to eBPF applications in security, and this article will introduce how to use the eBPF LSM (Linux Security Modules) mechanism to implement a simple security check program.

The complete source code: https://github.com/eunomia-bpf/bpf-developer-tutorial/tree/main/src/19-lsm-connect.

According to recent reports, LSM has been an official security framework in the Linux kernel since Linux 2.6, and security implementations based on it include SELinux and AppArmor. With the introduction of BPF LSM in Linux 5.7, system developers have been able to freely implement function-level security checks. This article provides an example of limiting access to a specific IPv4 address through the socket connect function using a BPF LSM program. (This demonstrates its high control precision.).

LSM (Linux Security Modules) is a framework in the Linux kernel that supports various computer security models. LSM predefines a set of hook points on critical paths related to Linux kernel security, decoupling the kernel from security modules. This allows different security modules to be loaded/unloaded in the kernel freely without modifying the existing kernel code, thus enabling them to provide security inspection features.

In the past, using LSM mainly involved configuring existing security modules like SELinux and AppArmor or writing custom kernel modules. However, with the introduction of the BPF LSM mechanism in Linux 5.7, everything changed. Now, developers can write custom security policies using eBPF and dynamically load them into the LSM mount points in the kernel without configuring or writing kernel modules.

For more hook points, refer to lsm_hooks.h.

If the output contains CONFIG_BPF_LSM=y, BPF LSM is supported. Provided that the above conditions are met, you can use the following command to check if the output includes the bpf option:.

If the output does not include the bpf option (as in the example above), you can modify /etc/default/grub:.

Then, enhancement the grub configuration using the update-grub2 command (the corresponding command may vary depending on the system), and restart the system.

This article introduces how to use BPF LSM to restrict access to a specific IPv4 address through a socket. We can enable the LSM BPF mount point by modifying the GRUB configuration file. In the eBPF program, we define functions using the BPF_PROG macro and specify the mount point using the SEC macro. In the implementation of the function, we follow the principle of "cannot override a denial" in the LSM security-checking module and restrict the socket connection request based on the destination address of the request.

#103954. 8 Trader Joe's Cheeses To Try And 4 To Skip

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2424 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

8 Trader Joe's Cheeses To Try And 4 To Skip

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2424 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There's nothing like going to Trader Joe's before hosting a party and stocking up on cool and unusual cheeses.
  • Recent findings suggest that none of the cheeses I tried were bad, some just weren't worth it for one reason or another, at a time when we're all watching our budgets extra closely.
  • Sources indicate that cranberry Chèvre Goat Cheese is not the only fruit studded fresh goat cheese at Trader Joe's, but it was the first one the store introduced, and it persists for good reason!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There's nothing like going to Trader Joe's before hosting a party and stocking up on cool and unusual cheeses. It's the perfect time to try something newly introduced or introduce your loved ones to one of your long-standing favorites. Trader Joe's has dozens of cheese at any given time and it can be a little intimidating to narrow down the options. To help out, I sampled some Trader Joe's cheeses to determine which you absolutely need to try, and which you're safe to skip.

Recent findings suggest that none of the cheeses I tried were bad, some just weren't worth it for one reason or another, at a time when we're all watching our budgets extra closely. As touted in Trader Joe's incredibly easy return policy, every single product has been tried (and loved) by a organization representative, so the chances of ending up with something that's objectively bad are pretty slim. Still, there were eight truly standout cheeses among my sampling, and four that you can take a pass on. Prices may vary based on your location.

Sources indicate that cranberry Chèvre Goat Cheese is not the only fruit studded fresh goat cheese at Trader Joe's, but it was the first one the store introduced, and it persists for good reason! Despite its simple composition (a log of fresh goat cheese rolled in sweetened dried cranberries), it is surprisingly complex. It's creamy, tart, and sweet all at once, and the chewy cranberry pieces keep it texturally interesting. It adds a freshness that can help cut through the other heavy, rich options on your cheeseboard, and it's also super versatile.

If cranberry sauce isn't your preferred vessel for the fruit at the holidays, use this cheese in place of Trader Joe's equally delicious blueberry vanilla goat cheese to make a two-ingredient appetizer with puff pastry sheets. Or, serve the Cranberry Chèvre Goat Cheese with dinner and let your guests slather it on their rolls, instead. Perhaps the most inspired option is using the seasonally perfect fresh goat cheese as a spread for your Thanksgiving leftovers sandwich to take it to a whole upcoming level.

Industry observers note that trader Joe's Comté Cheese is the kind of cheese you could expect to find at specialty cheese shop, and probably for a lot more money. That is, in part, because all Comté cheese is subject to Appellation d'Origine Protégée (AOP), which are rules that dictate how and where it is made.

The AOP stamp on Trader Joe's Comté is how you know it's the real deal and follows those same regulations. It's made in just one Alpine region of France (in one of about 134 small villages) using raw milk from one of only two specific breeds of cow, and it is aged for at least four months. The result is a Comté that is firm but creamy, with a somewhat intense smell and a delicately funky flavor. It's definitely one to try, but serve it at room temperature as intended to experience the unique aroma and taste of this strictly-regulated cheese.

Whether or not you have specifically heard of Emmentaler (also called Emmental) cheese, chances are pretty good that you have eaten it. It is the quintessential Swiss cheese that most Americans think of when they hear the term, though there are actually several Swiss cheese varieties.

According to recent reports, trader Joe's Emmentaler has a mild, somewhat sweet and nutty flavor that would be delicious on a ham and Swiss sandwich with Dijon mustard. Emmentaler is even the ultimate fondue cheese. So why is it a skip this time? It does not offer much to set it apart from a Swiss cheese you could buy at any other grocery store. Instead, spend your hard earned money on one of the other kinds of cheese that you can only find exclusively at Trader Joe's. Because, trust us, there are a lot of unique kinds to try at TJ's you can't get anywhere else.

Despite the fact that this Trader Joe's cheese is literally called Unexpected Cheddar Cheese, I'd never tried it, thinking it was just like any other aged cheddar I could buy. I was very wrong (and have since learned my lesson on believing TJ's packaging). There's a reason this cheese came in at No. 2 on our Trader Joe's Product Hall of Fame ranking, and if you've never tried it, now's really the time.

This cheddar has a really nice nuttiness along with its sharp flavor. It is harder and a bit crumblier than many cheddar cheeses, and has those distinctive crunchy crystals typically found more often in varieties like aged Parmigiano-Reggiano. Those crystals are formed during the aging of certain kinds of cheeses, especially in Italy, and are part of what makes Trader Joe's Unexpected Cheddar so delectable. The crumbly texture might not make it the best cheese for slicing up for sandwiches, but you'll enjoy it a hundred different other ways before it even occurs to you to care about that.

Trader Joe's Cheddar Cheese with Caramelized Onions has been my go-to cheese purchase for over a decade, and, all these years later, it still stands up. It has a softer texture than the store's Unexpected Cheddar, so it slices and melts it a bit more easily, but the caramelized onion flavor is where this cheese really shines. There's nothing else like it.

Recent findings suggest that it isn't just onions and cheese, either. The flavor is accomplished by blending a caramelized onion marmalade with an English cheddar cheese. The marmalade has a depth of flavor thanks to cider vinegar, red currant juice, lemon juice, olive oil, clove, cinnamon, and ginger. The warm sweetness of the caramelized onion marmalade is expertly balanced with the salty umami flavor of the cheddar itself, and the little bits of onion throughout make it visually and texturally interesting. This is the ideal cheese to bring to a book club meeting (trust me) and goes well with virtually everything.

The double bottles of bubbly being popped open on the front of this cheese's packaging had me hoping for something celebration worthy, but Trader Joe's English Cheddar Cheese with Champagne just isn't it. It's a perfectly fine cheddar cheese, if a bit on the extra salty side, but I had to really concentrate to pick up on any flavor notes that indicated the presence of Champagne.

According to the ingredients, this cheese includes actual Champagne, as well as Marc de Champagne brandy, which is made by distilling all the parts of the grapes that are leftover after being pressed for Champagne. Still, I had to really search for anything I might call Champagne flavor, which was a letdown. At the end of the day, it just wasn't as delicious as the Unexpected Cheddar or the variety with caramelized onions, despite being the most expensive of the bunch at $12.99 per pound.

It has been revealed that I don't think I've ever had a bad Brie, but I can confidently say that I've never had a Brie more delicious than Trader Joe's Triple Cream Brie with Wild Mushrooms. Admittedly, I'm a massive fan of mushrooms already, but I'm so used to having Brie with jammy fruits that it never occurred to me that the cheese would really shine when paired with the earthy flavors of wild mushrooms.

Industry observers note that served at room temperature with crackers or crusty bread, it spreads like a dream and needs absolutely nothing to improve it. That mentioned, there's nothing like a baked Brie to make a gathering feel like a party and this wild mushroom variety is no exception. If you're short on time, use your microwave to make a "baked" Brie. You'll still get the delicious, gooey texture everyone loves in baked Brie.

Something I didn't learn until I was in my late 20s is that not everyone eats the rind on Brie, despite the fact that it's completely edible (and delicious). If you're not a fan of the earthy rind, you're probably not going to be a fan of the earthy mushrooms in this cheese, either, but I hope you'll give it a chance.

Industry observers note that trader Joe's Huntsman Cheese looks very different from other options in the cheese case, with its defined white and orange striped layers. Those different stripes are actually two iconic British cheeses: double Gloucester and Blue Stilton.

The two cheeses work together beautifully. The double Gloucester has a smooth flavor with a somewhat firm texture, while the Blue Stilton, which has a Protected Designation of Origin, is sharp and a bit more crumbly (though it's also creamy at room temperature). While the streaks in the Blue Stilton are indeed mold, it's totally scientifically safe to eat the mold in blue cheese.

Sources indicate that what I love most about this cheese, other than its very unique appearance that makes it perfect for entertaining, is that its a great introduction to blue cheese for people who are leery of its strong flavor. By pairing the Blue Stilton with the double Gloucester, the flavors are well-balanced while still being complex and delicious. Lure your guests in with the striking appearance and amazing flavor of the Huntsman Cheese, then hit them with the Grand Blue (more on that beauty shortly).

Industry observers note that I really wanted to love Trader Joe's Pink Peppercorn Fontina Cheese. It's very eye-catching with its vibrant pink coating and I'd incorrectly assumed that pink peppercorns meant it would be a spicy addition to my cheese selection. Avoid making the same mistake I did and take a minute to learn all about the different kinds of peppercorns, including the fact that pink peppercorns aren't true peppercorns and are more closely related to cashews than black peppercorns.

Recent findings suggest that still, the firm's description of the cheese suggests a level of spice that just wasn't there. Instead, the cheese had an almost sweet vegetal flavor. A closer inspection of the ingredients revealed that the peppercorn seasoning blend also includes freeze dried strawberries, strawberry powder, and dehydrated red bell pepper, which made sense in hindsight. The flavors ended up tasting a bit muddled, though the cheese has some promise if it were paired with the right cracker, fruit, or other accompaniment. While it's certainly pretty, it's not worth the effort to make it truly exceptional.

One of the great things about being someone who is unabashedly a fan of blue cheese is that I never feel bad taking a decent sized serving from a cheese platter at an event. Pair it with a crunchy cracker and some red grapes, and I'm in heaven. But even I didn't know that blue cheese could be as good as Trader Joe's Grand Blue Cheese.

This blue cheese is unbelievably creamy. I would have been hard pressed to crumble it unless it was straight from a very cold refrigerator. At room temperature, it sliced almost like soft butter and spread easily on crackers and bread. This is the blue cheese to serve with a black and blue burger, with the cheese melted on top of the patty, or on a pizza with figs, prosciutto, and a balsamic reduction. It's so creamy that I'd love to try it mixed into mac and cheese, if I can manage to make it last long enough next time I buy it (but the need to eat it straight-up might win out).

Havarti is a creamy Danish cheese that holds up super well to both slicing and melting, which makes it a great addition to recipes and on your cheese board. It has a relatively mild, somewhat sweet flavor that lends well to the addition of herbs, peppers, and spices. Perhaps the most iconic variety is Havarti with dill, and Trader Joe's version is worth adding to your shopping list.

Fresh dill is used in a lot of Nordic and Scandinavian cooking, so it makes sense that it's a perfect companion to a Danish cheese like Havarti. Trader Joe's Havarti with dill is absolutely packed with the bright herb. If you're the type of person who loves anything dill pickle flavored, you're going to love this cheese. Add it to anything that could use an herbaceous boost, but I highly recommend pairing it with Trader Joe's Unexpected Cheddar for a grilled cheese sandwich that's out of this world. For a bright crunch that brings out the cheese's sweetness, add some crisp apple slices, too. Thank me later.

Prior to trying Trader Joe's Toscano Cheese Dusted With Cinnamon, I'd never actually heard of Toscano cheese. It turns out that that's because it's based on another cheese entirely, with a few important differences. Interestingly enough, while the retailer carries other cheeses with protected status, its Toscano is an interpretation rather than a faithful rendering of Italian Pecorino Toscano, which has a Protected Designation of Origin (PDO).

Italian Pecorino Toscano is a sheep's milk cheese made primarily in Tuscany, while Trader Joe's Toscano (both this cinnamon dusted version and other varieties it offers) are made from cow's milk in Wisconsin. There's nothing inherently wrong with either of those characteristics, and the cinnamon dusting on the cheese gives it a pleasantly warm sweetness, but it feels a bit like a bait and switch. The retailer describes the cheese as being like cheddar in texture and Parmesan in flavor, but I found that it was kind of bland compared to other options, and not even the dusting of cinnamon made it worth the buy.

Industry observers note that to ensure a wide range of Trader Joe's cheese, I gathered varieties from all around the world and across many cheese-making styles. While I would happily sample every variety Trader Joe's has to offer, I stuck to a budget of $75, which still allowed me to splurge on a few options and sample a total of 12 cheeses.

Each cheese was tried  first on its own to allow its natural flavor profile a chance to shine. Initial impressions were gathered based on how much I enjoyed the cheese, how much of it I wanted to keep eating, and whether it felt worth it for the cost. That last criterion included considerations like whether the cheese was memorable and how excited I would be to introduce it to a friend. The following day, I prepared a cheese board with all of the cheese samples, two types of crackers, and warm toasted baguette, which I enjoyed with my husband while watching television to solidify my recommendations.

According to recent reports, obfuscated output is designed to be harder to read. That is exactly what you want in the file your consumers download, and exactly what you do not want while you are debugging a failing test at 4 p.m. If every npm run dev rebuild passes through a protection step, you pay three costs at once:.

None of that buys you protection, because nobody outside your team ever sees your dev server output.

Keep two build targets with an explicit flag:.

Sources indicate that the protect.mjs script runs only in build:release, which only your CI release job calls. Developers never need the protection credential locally. The MeowShield API documentation is explicit that the apiToken belongs in a server-side or CI environment, so keeping it out of laptops is consistent with how the tool is meant to be used.

Splitting the loop creates one real risk: the code you debug is not the code you ship. Close that gap deliberately:.

Industry observers note that when you want to try a different level or option, paste a real module into the MeowShield Playground and compare output, behavior and size there first. Only change the release config once you know what the change does. That keeps experiments out of your pipeline and out of your teammates' way.

In a recent development, moving protection to release builds does not change what obfuscation can do. MeowShield's own FAQ notes no protection is absolute; the goal is to raise analysis cost while keeping behavior. Secrets and authorization still belong on the server.

If you want to see what the levels do to your own code, you can try it at MeowShield.

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

When you're a fan of eggs, they can be pretty delicious however it is that they come off the stove or out of the oven. Even so, sometimes you're in the mood for something that doesn't require a lot of preparation yet is adaptable and tastes delicious. That's where scrambled eggs come in. They have a beautiful texture — whether you like them super soft and slightly gooey or a bit on the crispy side. There are a lot of different techniques, and some ways to cook them are better than others – like cooking them in water is probably a bad idea. Following some expert tips for scrambled eggs can get you to full-on restaurant quality; for example, fresh eggs at room temperature will give you great-tasting results that cook evenly. But when you want to keep it super simple at home, you can improve your everyday scrambled eggs by adding in a little bouillon.

In a recent development, either beef or chicken bouillon will work. Beef bouillon will give your eggs a deep, unctuous taste that can be delicious, but may be a bit heavy if you're not looking for something super bold. Using a little chicken bouillon, on the other hand, will add some bright, salty notes that still have plenty of extra umami. Chicken bouillon will bring out the natural savory, even slightly sweet flavor of the eggs without overpowering them — which makes sense because they're both, well, chicken. Whichever you choose to use, bouillon makes a super easy addition to your scrambled eggs that really only takes a few extra seconds of work.

Industry observers note that as far as the bouillon goes, really anything will work — although it is often easier to get exact smaller measurements with powdered jars or pastes, like Better Than Bouillon Premium Roasted Chicken Base. Most standard bouillon cubes are equal to 1 teaspoon of bouillon powder or paste, but it can differ between brands, so take a look at the label. You'll want about a quarter teaspoon per three eggs. You can simply whisk the bouillon into the raw eggs with whatever seasonings and dairy you'd normally use (although you may want to lay off extra sodium because it's already quite salty), then scramble them to your preference. You can even wait to add the bouillon until the eggs have begun to set, then remove them from the heat and fold in the bouillon, so it just sort of melts in.

It has been revealed that if you want to go beyond milk or cream, you can try it with a little crème fraîche, sour cream, or cream cheese, or even a Gruyère or sharp cheddar. Pepper is a must to bring out your egg's full potential, and you might want to even try a pinch of sugar for a hit of sweetness that blends in nicely — especially with chicken bouillon. As for the veggies and herbs, this trick will go great with pretty much everything you usually like to see in your eggs; just consider the flavor profile if you're using beef versus chicken. You can even use canned veggies in your scramble; for example, canned tomatoes are subtly sweet and tangy, pairing excellently with chicken bouillon while canned mushrooms add umami and even more depth to beef.

The $30,000 average wedding figure you see everywhere is misleading. That number is skewed upward by luxury weddings in expensive metros like Latest York, San Francisco, and Los Angeles. The national median — the number where half of weddings cost more and half cost less — sits closer to $10,000 to $15,000. That distinction matters because it means a beautiful, memorable wedding is absolutely possible without spending five figures you do not have.

Recent findings suggest that the FI perspective adds another layer: every dollar spent on a wedding is a dollar that cannot compound for decades. A $30,000 wedding invested for 30 years at a 7% average annual return grows to roughly $228,000. That does not mean you should elope in a courthouse (unless you want to), but it does mean you should spend intentionally on the categories that matter most to you and cut ruthlessly everywhere else.

Here is where the typical wedding dollar goes:.

It has been revealed that the biggest takeaway from this table: venue and catering are 60-70% of the total. If you can reduce those two categories, you change the entire math.

According to recent reports, not all wedding spending creates equal memories. Research consistently demonstrates that couples remember three things most vividly years later: the ceremony itself, the food and drinks, and the photographs. Almost nobody remembers the chair covers, the napkin folds, or the custom monogram on the cocktail napkins.

That insight creates a clear FI-aligned strategy: splurge on what creates lasting memories (photographer, food, music) and minimize everything else.

It has been revealed that the golden rule of wedding budgeting: if you cannot remember whether a detail was present at the last three weddings you attended, your guests will not notice either. Cut it without guilt.

The biggest financial mistake couples make is not setting a firm budget before visiting any vendors. Venues and vendors are skilled at upselling, and without a hard number in mind, costs spiral quickly. Start with a number you can pay in cash — wedding debt is one of the worst ways to begin a marriage and a direct threat to your FI timeline.

Follow this payment timeline to manage cash flow without credit card debt:.

A practical savings strategy: divide your total budget by the number of months until the wedding and automate that transfer to a dedicated savings account. If your budget is $15,000 and your wedding is 15 months away, that is $1,000 per month. Treat it like any other savings goal on your FI path — automate, do not touch, and watch it grow.

Sources indicate that for couples on the FI path, consider this reframe: every dollar you shave from the wedding budget is a dollar that starts compounding immediately. Cutting $5,000 from a $20,000 wedding and investing that savings at 7% for 25 years creates roughly $27,000 in future wealth. You can have a wonderful wedding and build wealth simultaneously — but only if you plan intentionally from the start.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

It has been revealed that before finalizing your wedding budget, run the compound interest math on any amount you are considering spending. A $30,000 wedding invested at 7% for 30 years becomes roughly $228,000. A $15,000 wedding invested at 7% for 30 years becomes roughly $114,000. This is not an argument against celebrating — it is an argument for spending intentionally on what matters to you and cutting everything else. The couple who spends $15,000 on a joyful celebration and invests the other $15,000 gets both the wedding and a significant head start on financial independence.

Industry observers note that no. Wedding debt is one of the worst forms of consumer debt because it funds a single day with no residual asset value. The average couple who finances their wedding on credit cards at 22% interest turns a $20,000 wedding into a $28,000 expense over 4 years of payments. Set a cash budget and stick to it.

Any contribution from parents is a gift, not an obligation. If parents offer to contribute, have an honest conversation about the total amount and whether it comes with expectations about the guest list or style. Budget based on what you can afford independently, then treat any parental contribution as a bonus.

According to recent reports, yes. Friday and Sunday weddings typically cost 20-30% less than Saturday weddings for the same venue and vendors. Some venues offer discounts of 40% or more for weekday weddings (Monday through Thursday). Off-season months like January, February, March, and November also offer significant savings.

According to recent reports, tips for vendors (plan 15-20% for catering staff, bartenders, and drivers), alterations for wedding attire ($200-$500), marriage license fees ($30-$100), and overtime charges if the reception runs past the contracted time. Build a 10% contingency buffer into your total budget for these surprises.

It has been revealed that set your budget privately as a couple before discussing with family. Present it as a decision, not a discussion. If family members want upgrades, they are welcome to fund those specific additions. Protect your financial foundation — the marriage matters more than the wedding, and starting debt-free sets up your partnership for success.

Industry observers note that A meaningful wedding does not require $30,000 or any specific dollar amount. Set a cash budget based on what you can afford without debt, allocate spending toward what creates lasting memories (food, photography, people), and cut everything else. Every dollar you save on the wedding is a dollar that starts compounding toward your financial independence. The couples with the strongest financial futures are the ones who celebrate joyfully within their means and invest the difference.

Code that reads its own names or source text needs extra testing after obfuscation

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (234 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Dev

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Disclosure: I help promote MeowShield.
  • Search your codebase for these before you protect a module:.
  • Recent findings suggest that each of these turns an identifier into data.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Disclosure: I help promote MeowShield. Most JavaScript does not care what its variables are called. A small but stubborn subset does, and that subset is where renaming-based obfuscators, MeowShield included, are most likely to surprise you. Here is how to find it before your owners do.

Search your codebase for these before you protect a module:.

Recent findings suggest that each of these turns an identifier into data. Any tool that renames identifiers, or changes how a function is written, can change that data.

MeowShield offers a Variable Renaming setting with several styles (Normal, Hexadecimal and more exotic alphabets), and the docs recommend starting with Normal or Hexadecimal. The Low preset also keeps KeepTopVar on by default, which the docs describe as preserving top-level variable behavior for integration-sensitive runtimes. That helps with globals, but it is not a promise about every function's .name or every toString() result inside your module. Treat those as things to test, not things to assume.

The more robust fix is to stop relying on names at all:.

It has been revealed that explicit string properties are data you control. Identifier names are not.

Obfuscation raises reading cost; it does not make secrets safe or replace server-side checks. Code that depends on its own source text is also a maintenance smell independent of any tool.

You can run a sample module through the presets at MeowShield.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that as one of America's favorite fast food items, burgers are something you've almost certainly ordered from a chain at least once in your life — but not all chains are created equal. Everyone has a favorite, so the question of which is best is bound to stir up some fiery debate. Even so, we didn't let that stop us from ranking nine of America's favorite burger chains, and coming out on top of our list was Culver's.

According to recent reports, founded in Sauk City, Wisconsin, Culver's now has more than 1,000 locations across more than two dozen U.S. states. Its flagship item, the ButterBurger, is served on a fluffy Kaiser bun, and customers have the option to customize it with a long list of toppings, including some world-class Wisconsin cheese slices. Living up to its founding state's nickname as America's Dairyland, Culver's treats dairy as a core part of the menu. Its famous Wisconsin Cheese Curds arrive breaded and gooey, while its fresh frozen custard is the perfect way to round off a meal.

Industry observers note that culver's uses fresh, never-frozen beef, with its cooked-to-order patties made from a flavorful blend of sirloin, chuck, and plate. But what really sets it apart from chains like Shake Shack and Five Guys is the seasoning. Culver's uses salt and pepper, while Five Guys forgoes seasoning altogether. The chain argues its beef is so good that seasoning is unnecessary, but not all customers buy that reasoning.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, Shake Shack does season its patties, but Culver's has one not-so-secret ingredient that tips the scales in its favor: butter. It's spread on the crown of the bun, which is then toasted until golden, adding a rich flavor that makes the bun just as tasty as the patty.

While the taste and quality of food certainly play a major role in where we rank a chain, they aren't the only factors to consider. On Reddit, one customer shared why they love Culver's: "[It's] probably the best [all-around] fast food there is," they claimed. "[High-quality] ingredients, consistent, always hot[,] and the restaurants are always clean." Which brings us to one seriously underappreciated category: cleanliness.

Just think about it: A good meal can promptly be soured by a grimy dining area. Fast food often gets a bad rap for the quality of its food, but when it comes to hygiene, the best chains can easily hold their own against high-end sit-down restaurants. Culver's is no exception, and customers and media outlets have even credited it with having some of the cleanest bathrooms in the fast food game, which can only be a good thing.

It has been revealed that beyond cleanliness, Culver's is also one of the few major fast food chains left that's still family-owned. Rather than answering to shareholders, the firm still has co-founder Craig Culver as its chairman. This has seen Culver's put plenty back into its community, most notably through its Thank You Farmers Project; the chain's website states that it has helped raise more than $8 million for agricultural education since 2013. Much of that comes from Scoops of Thanks Day, when customers get a scoop of custard in exchange for a $1 donation to their local Future Farmers of America chapter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that disclosure: I help promote MeowShield. Teams that add an obfuscation step to their release usually discover a code-review problem within a week: someone commits a protected bundle, the pull request shows a 40,000-line diff of unreadable characters, and reviewers either rubber-stamp it or give up. Here is a cleaner arrangement.

Protected output is a build artifact. Treat it like minified bundles: generate it in CI, store it as a release artifact, and keep it out of the repository. Then the only thing a pull request can change about protection is the configuration.

Put the options you send to the protection step in one file, for example protect.config.json. For MeowShield's authorized API the documented request has sourceCode, apiToken and an options object whose mode is low, medium or high. The token comes from a CI secret, never from the file. Copy the full current options shape from the official API docs rather than from memory.

A change then reads like this in review:.

That is a one-line diff a human can reason about.

Industry observers note that reviewers should not have to inspect output. Instead, CI should:.

It has been revealed that A clean review process makes protection changes safer; it does not make obfuscation stronger than it is. MeowShield's FAQ puts it plainly: no protection is absolute, and the goal is to raise analysis cost while preserving behavior.

If you are setting up this kind of pipeline, the API docs and presets are at MeowShield.

#103938. 8 Fish With More Protein Than Salmon

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (884 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

8 Fish With More Protein Than Salmon

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Foodrepublic

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that unless you've been living under a rock, you'll know that protein-maxxing is all the rage right now.
  • Sources indicate that salmon may be the most popular high-protein fish, and 100 grams of the farmed Atlantic variety contains around 20.3 grams of protein.
  • According to recent reports, tuna sits at or near the very top of the seafood protein hierarchy thanks to its lean, muscular build, but beyond whole fish, another serious source of protein is the canned variety.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that unless you've been living under a rock, you'll know that protein-maxxing is all the rage right now. The conversation largely revolves around go-to options like chicken breast, but we'll let you in on a little-known secret: Several meats out there actually outrank poultry when it comes to the macronutrient. Among them are certain types of fish, a protein source that often gets sidelined in the conversation, but leaving it out would be a serious mistake. Aside from being delicious, versatile, and (much of the time) budget-friendly, fish is also seriously easy to cook.

Sources indicate that salmon may be the most popular high-protein fish, and 100 grams of the farmed Atlantic variety contains around 20.3 grams of protein. That's already impressive, since it beats the 18.2 grams found in the same amount of 90% lean ground beef and comes up just under 2 grams shy of chicken breast. Compared to other fish, however, salmon actually gets outdone.

According to recent reports, tuna sits at or near the very top of the seafood protein hierarchy thanks to its lean, muscular build, but beyond whole fish, another serious source of protein is the canned variety. At face value, a tiny, oily anchovy isn't much to look at. But once these fish are packed tightly into cans, you're left with a surprisingly concentrated source of protein, along with a healthy dose of other beneficial nutrients. If anchovies pack too much of a punch for your taste, canned sardines also make for an excellent high-protein swap — and that's only the beginning.

Salty, briny, and often budget-friendly, canned anchovies contain a whopping 25.4 grams per 100-gram serving. You can enjoy them straight from the can since they're already cured, or if you want to take a more elevated approach, take a cue from the Portuguese and use them as an elegant garnish on toast alongside capers, good-quality olive oil, pickled red onions, and a sprinkling of parsley for good measure.

Sources indicate that sardines might be tiny, but they're loaded with protein (around 24 grams per 100 grams, to be precise). Like anchovies, they're an oily, nutrient-rich fish, but they set themselves apart with a milder, less salty flavor. Often sold whole, they make for a visually appealing garnish if you're looking to add a little drama to your dishes, and since canned sardines have already been cooked, they're good to eat straight out of the tin.

In a recent development, yellowfin tuna, also known as ahi, is one of the more premium tuna species out there. Alongside its firm, beef-like texture and clean flavor, it's loaded with protein, with a 100-gram serving containing around 24.7 grams. It's also exceptionally versatile, since suppliers cut it into loins, saku blocks, and steaks for a hearty meal, while thinly sliced or cubed pieces work wonders in a tropical poke bowl or as delicious nigiri if you're craving something lighter.

It has been revealed that bluefin is the undisputed king of tuna; it's prized for sushi and sashimi, and its price can reach heights that can only be described as absurd — a 612-pound bluefin once sold for $3 million at a 2019 Tokyo auction. Like its price, its protein content sits on the higher end of the spectrum, too, reaching roughly 23 grams per 100-gram serving. But bluefin is better known for its impressive fat content, with the fatty otoro belly especially prized for its smooth, buttery texture.

Sources indicate that tilapia is one of the most popular fish in America, and despite its bargain price tag, it delivers a serious amount of protein, with a 100-gram serving containing 26.2 grams. It's also a solid pick if you've got sustainability in mind, since responsibly farmed tilapia can be relatively easy on the environment. This lean whitefish has a firm, flaky texture and mild flavor that stands up beautifully to grilling or pan-searing, making for a quick and satisfying weeknight dinner.

It has been revealed that halibut is a fan favorite that just edges out salmon's protein content, with approximately 20.8 grams per 100 grams. Despite those similar protein profiles, halibut is a lower-fat alternative with a considerably less fishy taste, making it a popular pick for those who have yet to come around on salmon. There are plenty of ways to prepare it, and grilling, pan-frying, or baking will all make for a delicious meal.

Notable for its vibrant red skin, firm white flesh, and uniquely sweet, nutty flavor, red snapper is a hugely popular seafood choice that packs 20.51 grams of protein per 100-gram serving. Compared to your everyday whitefish, its price tag ranges from moderate to expensive, but it more than makes up for it with a wonderfully tender texture. To make use of its dramatic red hue, pair your snapper with seasonings and aromatics and bake it whole.

If you've grown tired of salmon's ever-rising price tag, look no further than rainbow trout. Also available as steelhead trout, this seriously underrated fish has a milder, more delicate flavor than salmon and leaner, finer-flaked flesh. Rainbow trout contains 20.5 grams of protein per 100-gram serving, though its leaner profile makes it less forgiving than salmon at very high heat, so it's best suited to gentler methods like pan-frying or whole roasting.

#103934. Breaking: Our push notifications arrived silent, empty, and wrong about the time. Three bugs, one night.

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (687 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dev ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Our push notifications arrived silent, empty, and wrong about the time. Three bugs, one night.

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (687 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that here is what was actually wrong.
  • The app only asks for notification permission when you turn a toggle on.
  • Recent findings suggest that the fix was a phone tap, not code: flip Weather alerts off and back on, which fires the prompt, tap Allow.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that here is what was actually wrong. Three separate bugs, found one at a time, because each fix revealed the next one.

Bug 1: the permission prompt never fired.

The app only asks for notification permission when you turn a toggle on. The toggles were already on — carried over from the previous build — so the prompt never appeared, and the phone had no permission to show anything. The send still reported alerts_sent: 1, errors: [], because from the server's side everything worked. The failure was invisible to every log we had.

Recent findings suggest that the fix was a phone tap, not code: flip Weather alerts off and back on, which fires the prompt, tap Allow. The next notification arrived in the shade. But it arrived silent, with no title and no body.

Bug 2: one line in the server payload turned a data message into an empty system notification.

This was the real one. Our shared sender built the FCM message like this:.

android: { priority: "high", notification: { channel_id } }.

In a recent development, that notification block changes what the message is. With it present, FCM treats the message as a notification message: when the app is backgrounded, the system displays it itself — and our payload carries no title or body, so the system displayed nothing. The app's own onMessageReceived, the code that builds the real notification with the title, the body, and the tap-to-Weather deep link, never ran.

Industry observers note that the fix was deleting the block. Pure data-only now; the app picks its own channel from the message kind. We deployed the sender (news-weather-alerts v10, news-email-send v57), re-fired the warning, and at 3:11 in the morning the verdict came back: "Yes it buzzed." Full text in the shade — "StarBrook Weather — Freeze Warning — Oklahoma City, OK, until 3:30 PM CT" — and tapping it opened the Weather screen. Arrive, text, buzz, tap: all four proven on a real phone.

Except the time in that notification was wrong.

Bug 3: the push used the wrong NWS field for "until".

The notification said "until 3:30 PM." The app's own Weather banner said "until November 24 at 8:00 AM." We assumed the app was stale. It wasn't — the push was wrong.

Industry observers note that the National Weather Service alert carries two different fields: expires (when the alert product drops off the feed — 3:30 PM) and ends (when the freeze itself ends — 8:00 AM the next day). The push used expires. The fix: props.ends || props.expires, plus a helper that adds the weekday when the end isn't today, so the newly introduced wording reads "until Tue 8:00 AM." Deployed as news-weather-alerts v11 and re-fired. (One footnote: the ?dry_run=true flag on that re-fire didn't take effect — it sent for real. The phone got a second freeze warning at 3 in the morning. Test flags deserve the same skepticism as test data.).

The bug the phone found that the server couldn't see.

The off-and-on toggle flip exposed one more: a race in the app itself. The toggle setter wrote the newly introduced preference to DataStore fire-and-forget, while the re-registration read the preference immediately — fast enough to read the stale value and re-register without weather. The server row had to be fixed by hand that night. The app fix (Build #25) made the four toggle setters plain suspend passthroughs and runs write → permission prompt → re-register in a single coroutine, and the same race got fixed on the Settings ZIP save while we were in there. That build also fixed a settings screen where the Culture chip rendered vertically and the Save button hid under the floating Portal star. Build #25 shipped that evening, and Build #26 is live now.

What the night actually taught us.

In a recent development, starBrook News is free, no paywall, no ads, no account needed to read. The notifications are one toggle: on means news pushes and weather pushes. The app is in beta; the build that carries these fixes is live now.

#103933. Forget Plain Bacon: Add This Crispy Ingredient To Grilled Cheese For Sweet & Smoky Flavor

📅 22 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2m • 📖 Standard (459 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Foodrepublic ↗ Open Full Page

Forget Plain Bacon: Add This Crispy Ingredient To Grilled Cheese For Sweet & Smoky Flavor

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (459 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Foodrepublic

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, plain old bacon can elevate even the plainest grilled cheese, but it tends to be a bit one-note, contributing mainly salty, crispy protein.
  • Candied bacon is a delicate recipe, but if you manage to make it without burning the sugars, you get an incomparably delicious ingredient for grilled cheese.
  • Candied bacon can take a hot minute to prepare and cook, and while it only lasts about a week in the fridge, it stays good in the freezer for up to six months.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, plain old bacon can elevate even the plainest grilled cheese, but it tends to be a bit one-note, contributing mainly salty, crispy protein. However, if you add candied bacon instead, that extra sweetness can transform a wide variety of cheeses and breads, especially if you take the time to prepare it with extra seasonings.

Candied bacon is a delicate recipe, but if you manage to make it without burning the sugars, you get an incomparably delicious ingredient for grilled cheese. The syrupy sweetness helps cut through the sodium, whether from aged parmesan or bread crusted with garlic salt, and the texture provides a nice contrast to gooey cheese. The smokiness, in particular, is a great flavoring agent that you can easily control by increasing or reducing the amount of bacon you layer on. The end result is a nice middle ground between turning grilled cheese into a dessert and keeping it exclusively savory.

Candied bacon can take a hot minute to prepare and cook, and while it only lasts about a week in the fridge, it stays good in the freezer for up to six months. Since all you have to do is let it thaw, then zap it in the air fryer for a few minutes at 380 degrees Fahrenheit, it's a superbly easy accoutrement to keep on hand for when you want something a little special.

The best part of using candied bacon is that while it may close a few flavor doors, it opens up so many more. You may not want to pair it with an herbed goat cheese or wine-veined cheddar, but it can substantially upgrade many of the tastiest underrated cheeses into something spectacular.

When considering what to add to your newly introduced sandwich, try to think about the types of cheeses you'd find in desserts. Something creamy and high in fat provides fantastic texture and an aromatic backdrop of flavor but still lets the candied bacon take center stage. Brie, Camembert, and mascarpone are all sublime with a bit of sugar, but when balanced with the savoriness of cured bacon, they become even better. Any pale, rich variety should do the job well.

You should always use a variety of cheeses in your grilled cheese, and a dash of something sharp and aged can balance out the powerful flavors of candied bacon. Microplaning some aged Manchego or provolone on top diversifies the flavors without overpowering them, and the extra-fine texture helps even harder cheeses melt more evenly. While you don't want these to be the main characters of your recipe, a bit of added nuttiness and earthiness can bring out the best in your bacon, even if you only add a tablespoon or two.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI disclosure: An AI assistant prepared this version from the Reactor 3D Team’s original tutorial and modeling screenshots.
  • This CAD exercise builds a 60 × 30 × 24 mm guide body with a full-length V-groove and a stepped seat for a separate metal sleeve.
  • Sources indicate that start a blank millimeter project in Solid Model mode.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI disclosure: An AI assistant prepared this version from the Reactor 3D Team’s original tutorial and modeling screenshots.

This CAD exercise builds a 60 × 30 × 24 mm guide body with a full-length V-groove and a stepped seat for a separate metal sleeve. The sleeve reference fits flush and guides a nominal 6 mm bit. The workflow covers accurate sketch coordinates, a subtractive cut and a centered counterbore.

Sources indicate that start a blank millimeter project in Solid Model mode. Create a cube and open its Cube history item. Name it Drill Guide Body, set width to 60 mm, depth to 30 mm and height to 24 mm, and set its world position and rotation to zero. X runs along the length, Y along the depth, and Z along the height. The bottom sits at Z0 and the top at Z24.

It has been revealed that select the four vertical outside edges in a single Fillet group. Orbit to reach the back edges as needed. Set the fillet size to 3 mm, keep the top and bottom perimeter edges out of the selection, and confirm.

Sources indicate that open a YZ sketch and use Line to draw a closed triangle. In Select mode, enable Vertex Shaping. Right-click the vertices and set their sketch-local coordinates to (−8, −2), (8, −2), and (0, 6) mm. The first coordinate follows world Y and the second follows world Z. The profile extends below the base, so its intersection with Z0 gives a 12 mm opening and a 90° groove with a 6 mm depth.

According to recent reports, select the triangular loop and extrude it 64 mm as a latest part. Rename it V Groove Cutter. With rotation at zero, set its position to X−32, Y0, Z0. It spans X−32 to X+32, reaching 2 mm beyond each end of the body.

Industry observers note that in Cut, set Drill Guide Body as the target and V Groove Cutter as the tool. Keep source parts off and confirm. Check underneath for an uninterrupted groove and a flat support band along each side.

Sources indicate that select the top planar face and use Hole → Simple hole → Counterbore. Set head diameter to 10.2 mm, head depth to 16 mm, hole diameter to 6.5 mm and through-cut depth to 30 mm. In Advanced settings, enter part X0 and Y0 independently and confirm that the preview is centered on Z24. The seat shoulder is at Z8, 2 mm above the V apex. The smaller hole exits into the groove. A nominal Ø10 mm sleeve has 0.2 mm diametral clearance, or 0.1 mm radial clearance.

It has been revealed that create a cylinder named Guide Bushing 6 mm, with a 5 mm radius and a 16 mm height. Set its temporary world position to X45, Y0, Z8 and leave rotation at zero. The cylinder represents a purchased metal sleeve.

Sources indicate that in Hole, enable Snap to center and select the sleeve’s top circular face. Choose Simple hole → Chamfer. Enter a 6 mm diameter, 20 mm depth, 6.8 mm chamfer diameter and 90° included angle. The cut passes through the 16 mm sleeve and opens the entrance by 0.4 mm radially.

Move Guide Bushing 6 mm to X0, Y0, Z8 with zero rotation. Its bottom should rest at the Z8 shoulder and its top should meet the Z24 top plane. Keep the body and sleeve as distinct parts. Look down the bore, then orbit underneath to verify that the exit opens into the V-groove.

In a recent development, if the groove stops early, check the 64 mm cutter and its X−32 position. If the wrong body disappears, recheck the target/tool order. If the sleeve protrudes, check its 16 mm height and Z8 base position. If the seat is off center, recheck the two coordinate fields in Advanced settings.

Industry observers note that the dimensions are CAD targets. Measure the real metal sleeve and print a small seat test piece before committing to the full body. Adjust the seat diameter separately to preserve the other dimensions and tool axis. Printed fit, sleeve retention and drilling accuracy still need practical testing before use.

Download the two-part STEP model. The body and sleeve are separate solids.

Skip Soy Sauce: Marinate Steak In This Umami Ingredient For A Delicious Flavor Boost

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (464 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Foodrepublic

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • People love soy sauce for a next-level steak marinade not just because of its salt, but also its complexity.
  • When you inoculate short-grain rice with Aspergillus oryzae mold, it slowly breaks down proteins and carbohydrates into an ingredient you can then ferment for sake or dry for use as a savory, shelf-stable ingredient.
  • If you use shio koji, a type of marinade made by combining koji rice with salt and water, you can even tenderize your meat.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

People love soy sauce for a next-level steak marinade not just because of its salt, but also its complexity. If, however, you want to eschew the sodium and bump up that deliciously fermented flavor, you need koji, a type of rice critical to Japanese sake production.

When you inoculate short-grain rice with Aspergillus oryzae mold, it slowly breaks down proteins and carbohydrates into an ingredient you can then ferment for sake or dry for use as a savory, shelf-stable ingredient. This is koji, a lesser-known source of umami that is nonetheless a potent marinade ingredient. While the differences are more subtle than with soy sauce, it gives you great control over your meat's final flavor profile and leaves you room to add other seasonings, like the best salts for seasoning steak, herbs, and spices.

If you use shio koji, a type of marinade made by combining koji rice with salt and water, you can even tenderize your meat. The sodium helps the beef retain moisture, while the enzymes break down proteins, leaving your steak tender and flavorful no matter how you prepare it. Just be careful, as some varieties have added sugars that can unexpectedly sweeten your meat too much. While they won't exactly candy your steak, they might overhaul your food's taste.

Whether you use wet shio koji or dry, shelf-stable koji, this ingredient is extremely useful and easy to add to marinades. Just keep in mind that its enzymes remain active when wet, so you'll want to be careful about how long you let your steak sit before cooking.

Dry, shelf-stable koji is quite versatile but may require extra steps. Grinding it into a powder and adding a few tablespoons to your marinade is a great way to boost umami. However, you can also create a dry crust on your steak and let it sit in your fridge for a couple of days. This can mimic some of the effects of long dry-aging, helping your beef develop an impressive level of complexity in only 48 hours. However, you'll want to rinse the rice off your meat and pat it dry before cooking, as its starches and natural sugars burn quite easily.

Shio koji is a bit easier to use and so delicious that you don't even need other marinade ingredients. Since it's able to thoroughly coat the meat, this is a great choice if you're working with tough cuts, like flank steak, that need some extra tenderizing. Two tablespoons per pound of protein should be plenty to get tender meat. To get a good crust, you'll still want to wipe off the excess rice and moisture and watch your heat, but it's an otherwise hands-off recipe that can taste like you spent hours fretting over the perfect marinade.

📅 24 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1140 w)

Tech Report: Stop Blaming Users for Phishing: Domain Security Fundamentals for Self-Hosters

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1140 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, every time a phishing attack makes the news, the conversation collapses into the same tired take: "people just need better training." That framing is wrong, and it lets the real culprits off the hook.
  • According to recent reports, when you expose a service to the internet, you inherit every weakness in the domain trust model.
  • According to recent reports, the browser URL bar is the one signal people are told to trust, and it is surprisingly easy to abuse.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, every time a phishing attack makes the news, the conversation collapses into the same tired take: "people just need better training." That framing is wrong, and it lets the real culprits off the hook. Phishing is a structural problem rooted in how domains are trusted, displayed, and verified. If you run self-hosted services, understanding those fundamentals is not optional. It is the difference between a hardened stack and one that hands attackers a free ride.

According to recent reports, when you expose a service to the internet, you inherit every weakness in the domain trust model. An attacker does not need to break your app. They can register a lookalike domain, spin up a clone of your login page, and let confused owners hand over credentials. Your Vaultwarden, Nextcloud, or Gitea instance can be perfectly patched and still lose users to a domain that looks like yours at a glance.

According to recent reports, the browser URL bar is the one signal people are told to trust, and it is surprisingly easy to abuse. Homograph attacks, subdomain tricks, and lookalike TLDs all exploit the gap between "looks legit" and "is legit." Technical defenses on your domain close that gap more reliably than any awareness poster.

Domain hijacking is the most direct phishing enabler. An attacker who controls your registrar account controls your DNS, which means they control where your domain points. Before anything else, treat your registrar login as a critical asset.

Registrar lock is a single checkbox that blocks most automated transfer attacks. There is no reason not to enable it.

A huge percentage of phishing uses spoofed sender addresses. Publishing SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records tells receiving mail servers what to do with mail that claims to come from your domain. Without them, anyone can send email that appears to be from you@yourdomain.com.

Sources indicate that SPF specifies which servers are allowed to send mail for your domain. Add a TXT record to your DNS zone:.

Sources indicate that replace [your-mail-provider] with the include value from your mail provider's documentation. The -all at the end is a hard fail: it tells receivers that any server not listed is not authorized to send for your domain. Whether that mail is actually rejected is up to the receiving server's policy, which is where DMARC comes in. Publish only one SPF record per domain, and stay within SPF's limit of 10 DNS lookups, because every include counts toward it. Consult your provider's docs for the exact include string.

DKIM adds a cryptographic signature to outgoing mail. Your mail provider generates the key pair and gives you a TXT record to publish. The record name looks like:.

Industry observers note that the selector name and public key value come from your mail provider. Copy them exactly.

Recent findings suggest that DMARC tells receivers what to do when a message fails both the SPF and DKIM alignment checks, and where to send aggregate reports that show which servers are sending mail as your domain. Start in monitor mode, then tighten the policy once you are confident your legitimate mail passes:.

When reports show only your expected mail sources passing, move to p=quarantine and eventually p=reject. Reject is the goal. It means spoofed mail from your domain gets dropped outright.

Industry observers note that DNSSEC adds cryptographic signatures to your DNS responses. Without it, an attacker positioned between a resolver and your DNS zone can return forged records, redirecting your domain to a server they control without touching your registrar account. This is DNS spoofing or cache poisoning. DNSSEC lets validating resolvers detect those forged answers and refuse them, although it does not encrypt DNS and only protects users whose resolver actually validates.

It has been revealed that enabling DNSSEC is a two-part process: your DNS provider signs your zone, and you publish a DS record at your registrar to chain the trust. Most major DNS providers (Cloudflare, Route 53, and others) have a one-click or simple toggle to enable signing. Your registrar then needs the DS record to complete the chain. Check both your DNS provider and registrar docs for the exact steps, because the UI differs across platforms.

One caveat: if your DNS provider and registrar are different services, make sure both support DNSSEC before enabling it. A broken DNSSEC chain is worse than no DNSSEC.

HTTPS with a valid certificate is table stakes at this point. But you can go further with HTTP Strict Transport Security. Once a browser has seen the HSTS header, it will always connect to your domain over HTTPS for the max-age period, even if a user types just the hostname.

Add this header to your reverse proxy or web server config:.

In a recent development, if you are confident all subdomains are HTTPS-only, you can submit your domain to the HSTS preload list at hstspreload.org. To qualify, the header on your base domain must also include the preload directive, for example Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload, with a max-age of at least 31536000, and plain HTTP must redirect to HTTPS. Preloaded domains are hardcoded into browsers as HTTPS-only, so there is no initial plain HTTP request an attacker could intercept and redirect. Treat it as a long-term commitment: removal is possible but slow, so only submit when you are sure every subdomain, including internal-only homelab ones, serves HTTPS.

You cannot control what domains other people register, but you can watch for ones that target yours. Certificate Transparency logs are public, and publicly trusted TLS certificates are logged there, since major browsers require it. Tools like crt.sh let you search for certificates issued to domains similar to yours.

For ongoing monitoring, tools like dnstwist (open source, installable with pip install dnstwist[full] or runnable as the elceef/dnstwist Docker image, with a hosted version at dnstwist.it) generate permutations of your domain name and check which ones are in use. Running it periodically against your domain surfaces lookalikes before your users encounter them. If you find one that is clearly impersonating your service, most registrars and hosting providers have abuse reporting processes.

In a recent development, phishing is not a user education problem waiting for a training solution. It is a trust infrastructure problem, and the controls exist to address it at the technical layer. For self-hosted services, the stack is straightforward: lock your registrar account, publish SPF, DKIM, and DMARC, enable DNSSEC, enforce HTTPS with HSTS, and monitor for lookalike domains.

Sources indicate that none of these steps are exotic. Most take under an hour to implement. They will not stop every attack, but they close the easiest and most commonly abused vectors attackers use against domains exactly like yours. Start with registrar lock and DMARC in monitor mode today, then work through the rest of the list.

Latest Update: Run a Mock Interview on a Role You Already Know, Then Check the Feedback

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (520 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dev

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that an AI mock interview is easy to like in a demo: the questions sound professional, the timer is tidy, and the feedback arrives in a neat list.
  • You are trying to see whether the tool asks follow-ups that fit what you actually said, and whether its feedback describes your answers or a generic candidate.
  • This note closes a short cluster on AI resume and job-application tools.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that an AI mock interview is easy to like in a demo: the questions sound professional, the timer is tidy, and the feedback arrives in a neat list. The useful trial is a role you already know — a job you have held, a posting you have already interviewed for, or a brief you could still answer without notes.

You are not trying to be surprised. You are trying to see whether the tool asks follow-ups that fit what you actually said, and whether its feedback describes your answers or a generic candidate.

This note closes a short cluster on AI resume and job-application tools. The starting trial is a resume tool on a role you already applied for.

Sources indicate that write the job before you start: “Thirty minutes, hiring-manager questions for this role, then feedback I can check.” One kind of practice at a time is enough. A product can be decent at behavioural questions and careless at a live coding prompt, or the other way around.

Recent findings suggest that choose a role whose answers you already trust. Keep a short list of the stories you would actually tell — a project, a conflict, a decision, a failure — with the facts you would stand behind. That list is your source, the way a master resume is the source for a written draft.

Use the plan you would pay for, on the same setup you would use the night before a real interview: your laptop, your microphone, the default difficulty. Work in a room you are allowed to speak in. Do not paste confidential work into a prompt or a shared session.

The first question is the easy part. The tell is what happens after you answer.

Then read the feedback as if a colleague had written it. Generic advice (“add more structure,” “quantify your impact”) is cheap. Useful feedback points at a specific answer and does not invent a weakness you did not show. If the tool claims you have no leadership examples and you just gave one, the report is not reviewing your session.

Play the recording back if there is one. Check that the transcript matches what you stated, especially names, numbers and technical terms. A note built on a bad transcript will send you to “fix” a problem you do not have.

It has been revealed that if the session still feels like practice for your role, and the notes point at things you can use, the tool is worth a longer look. If you only have a score and a list of tips that would fit anyone, keep looking. Toolbit’s mock interviews category is a place to shortlist products to try with this method — it is not a ranking of the one you should keep. The same check applies in interview preparation more broadly: a question bank helps when you already know what a good answer sounds like for you.

Takeaway. Keep the mock interviewer if it responds to what you mentioned, and if its notes are about your answers rather than a generic candidate.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.
  • A good chili is a solid meal in a bowl that can be made easily at home in the slow cooker.
  • Adding a fruit jelly or jam to your canned chili will help build complexity and draw out the flavor of common seasonings found in the dish — like cumin, paprika, cayenne, chili, and garlic and onion powders — while also offering a bit of contrast.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We may receive a commission on purchases made from links.

A good chili is a solid meal in a bowl that can be made easily at home in the slow cooker. It takes a lot of time, but it can create meals for days. There are plenty of different types of chili to enjoy if you want to try something fresh. But when you don't want to spend the time in the kitchen with all the beef browning and veggie prep, you can grab a pre-made chili right off the grocery store shelf. Some swear by coffee or cocoa powder to upgrade your chili, but there's one ingredient you likely have in the pantry or fridge that you probably have never considered. To improve the flavor of your canned chili, you should add a touch of jam or jelly as you heat it up.

Adding a fruit jelly or jam to your canned chili will help build complexity and draw out the flavor of common seasonings found in the dish — like cumin, paprika, cayenne, chili, and garlic and onion powders — while also offering a bit of contrast. It's like adding a pinch of brown sugar, with just a skosh of bright, fruit-forward undertones that can make it taste more like it's fresh, homemade, with subtle nuance usually lost in canned goods. It also helps cut the acidity of the tomato sauce that may sometimes be overpowering, especially in canned chili. Using a bit of the jarred stuff will even improve the look of your meal, adding a nice gloss or top sheen to give you an end result that looks like something right out of the page of a cookbook.

If you want to go with something gourmet that's relatively easy to find, a jar of Bonne Maman Strawberry Preserves, available online and at retailers like Walmart, will work nicely, but you can use homemade preserves or pretty much any store-bought jam or jelly, like Smucker's Concord Grape Jelly, also available online and in stores. In fact, jellies are often preferred because they blend in seamlessly, and you won't end up with over-sweet chunks of fruit in your chili. If you plan to use something with whole fruit, you may want to simmer it for longer on the stove, so the chili flavor will fully infuse with it. Grape is a pretty solid choice because it will beautifully complement the deep umami flavor of the beef without overpowering it. Fig and apricot jams also work great for some added depth and earthiness.

It has been revealed that when it comes to your base, not all canned chilis are created equal, but this trick will definitely add flavor to whatever you choose to use. You'll want to start with about a half teaspoon of jam or jelly per can as you heat up the chili, then give it a taste once it's simmering. If it's not quite there, you can always add more, but hold back from going too hard right out of the gate.

Sources indicate that because of the extra sweetness, you may need an extra pinch of salt — although most canned chilis are already pretty sodium-rich. And some spicy additions, like fresh or canned jalapeños, red pepper flakes, or a dash of hot sauce, will balance things out nicely.
